title: Porcine in vitro degradation characteristics of heat pretreated and multi‐enzyme predigested maize whole stillage
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

This study investigated effects of predigesting untreated and heat-pretreated (at 70 psi and 160 °C for 20 min) maize whole stillage (WS) with multi-enzyme products on porcine in vitro digestibility and fermentation characteristics. Untreated WS and heat-pretreated WS were undigested or predigested (at 55 °C for 12 h) with three multi-enzyme products (MTE1, MTE2 and MTE3) in a 2 × 4 arrangement. The MTE1 supplied xylanase, cellulase, β-glucanase and protease; MTE2 supplied xylanase, α-galactosidase and cellulase; and MTE3 supplied xylanase, β-glucanase and mannanase.

RESULTS

The in vitro digestibility (IVD) of dry matter (IVD-DM) and IVD of non-starch polysaccharides (IVD-NSP) for untreated WS were 0.734 and 0.350, respectively. Fermentation gas production for untreated WS was 192 mL g–1 DM. Heat-pretreatment increased (P < 0.05) IVD-DM, IVD-NSP and fermentation gas production for WS by 8.13%, 13.8% and 9.69%, respectively. Multi-enzyme predigestion improved (P < 0.05) IVD-DM, IVD-NSP and fermentation gas production for WS by 10.3%, 51.5% and 7.34%, respectively. The IVD-DM and fermentation gas production for untreated WS was unaffected by multi-enzyme type; however, these two response criteria for the heat-pretreated WS were greater (P < 0.05) for MTE2 than for MTE1 or MTE3.

CONCLUSION

The digestibility and fermentation of WS were improved by heat-pretreatment and multi-enzyme predigestion. The combination of heat-pretreatment and MTE2 predigestion was the most effective in improving digestibility and fermentation of WS. © 2026 The Author(s).
